id: home-hero

  Native HTML, native CSS, vanilla JavaScript. No build step, no package manager,
  no vendor lock-in. Structure and styling are fixed; the words are data.

### Tile: feature
description: The core principles.
id: home-why
title: Why it exists
items:
  - title: Zero dependencies
    body: Pure HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JS. Nothing to install, compile or bundle — the source is the site.
  - title: Breakpoint-free layout
    body: One auto-fit grid handles every screen. Container queries let a tile adapt to its own width, not the window.
  - title: Owned outright
    body: Plain files on any host. No platform decides whether your site stays online, and nothing to migrate away from.

### Tile: feature
description: How the model works.
id: home-model
title: How it works
items:
  - title: 1 · The plate
    body: A root container sets the atmosphere and the grid. Every page is one plate.
  - title: 2 · The tiles
    body: Self-contained sections — a hero, a card, a form. Duplicate, reorder or delete them with no cascading damage.
  - title: 3 · The data
    body: Copy, theme and images live in one content file. The HTML owns structure; the file owns the words.

## Page: Quickstart
path: /quickstart.html

### Tile: hero
description: Hand-build intro.
id: qs-hero
headline: Build it by hand
body: |
  No AI, no build step. Copy a starter page, paste tiles into it, put your words in
  a content file. A text editor and a browser are the whole toolchain.
actions:
  - label: See the tiles
    href: /tiles.html
    style: ghost

### Tile: feature
description: The four-step loop.
id: qs-loop
title: The loop
items:
  - title: 1 · Copy the starter
    body: Take templates/plate.html, rename it index.html. It already has the plate, the nav and the footer.
  - title: 2 · Paste a tile
    body: Pick a tile from the kit, paste its markup inside <main>.
  - title: 3 · Add the words
    body: Put the matching entry in content.json — same id as the markup's data-tile-id.
  - title: 4 · Refresh
    body: That is the whole cycle. Change a word in the JSON and watch it move.

### Tile: code
description: Serve it locally.
id: qs-serve
title: Serve it locally
language: bash
code: |
  cd my-site
  python3 -m http.server 8080
  # open http://localhost:8080
  #
  # A local server is needed so the page can fetch content.json.
  # Opening the file directly (file://) blocks that fetch — that is the
  # browser's security model, not a bug.

### Tile: feature
description: What you need / do not need.
id: qs-needs
title: What you need
items:
  - title: You need
    body: A text editor, a browser, and Python (or any static server) to preview locally. Some HTML and CSS familiarity helps.
  - title: You do not need
    body: Node, npm, a bundler, a framework, a build pipeline, or a hosting account to start.
  - title: Coming from a site builder?
    body: If you can drag a section onto a page, you can paste one. The mental model is three ideas — see the kit's primer.

### Tile: code
description: Lint the site before you ship.
id: qs-check
title: Check it
language: bash
code: |
  node tools/check-site.mjs public

  # Verifies, with no browser:
  #   every data-tile-id has an entry in content.json
  #   every config key has a data-role slot or a data-* attribute
  #   every internal link and referenced file resolves
  #   every asset:<key> exists in the assets map

### Tile: content-card
description: Where the templates live.
id: qs-kit
headline: The two files that teach it
body: plate.html is the starter; TILE-KIT.md holds every tile's markup and its content entry, ready to copy.
actions:
  - label: Open the tile kit
    href: https://github.com/MaryTheadoor/nown-sites/blob/main/templates/TILE-KIT.md
    style: ghost

### Tile: cta
description: Deploy pointer.
id: qs-cta
headline: Ship it anywhere
body: Copy the folder plus the framework files, upload to Firebase Hosting, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Netlify or IPFS. Nothing to build.

## Page: Docs
path: /docs.html

### Tile: hero
description: The standard.
id: docs-hero
headline: The standard
body: |
  S.I.T.E.S is a specification, not a library. These are the rules a compliant site
  follows — everything on this site obeys them.
actions:
  - label: Read the full spec
    href: https://github.com/MaryTheadoor/nown-sites/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md
    style: gold

### Tile: feature
description: The hard rules.
id: docs-rules
title: The hard rules
items:
  - title: No build step
    body: Plain .html, .css and .js. No bundler, no package manager, nothing to compile — the source is the site.
  - title: Tokens, never literals
    body: Every colour, space, radius and shadow comes from a CSS custom property. That is what makes re-theming instant.
  - title: Breakpoint-free layout
    body: One auto-fit grid handles the macro layout; container queries let a tile adapt to its own width, not the window.
  - title: Copy is data
    body: Editable words live in the content file and bind into slots. The HTML owns structure only.
  - title: Progressive by default
    body: The page reads correctly with JavaScript disabled; behaviour is layered on top.
  - title: Services, not vendors
    body: Forms, maps, payments and AI are swappable adapters selected by configuration — never hard-coded into a tile.

### Tile: code
description: The whole responsive system.
id: docs-grid
title: The whole responsive system
language: css
code: |
  /* macro layout — no media queries */
  .sites-grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(300px, 1fr));
    gap: 1.5rem;
  }

  /* micro layout — a tile that knows its own width */
  .tile { container-type: inline-size; }
  @container (min-width: 720px) { .tile-hero:has(.media) { grid-template-columns: 1.1fr .9fr; } }

### Tile: feature
description: Conformance levels.
id: docs-levels
title: Conformance
items:
  - title: L1 Structural
    body: The plate and tiles model, with tiles built to the naming and data contract.
  - title: L2 Presentation
    body: Full tokenization, breakpoint-free layout, accessible and progressive.
  - title: L3 Content-managed
    body: Copy externalised to a schema-valid content file, editable from the admin.
  - title: L4 Managed and sovereign
    body: L3 plus a portable storage adapter and no third-party trackers. This site targets L4.

### Tile: faq
description: Common questions.
id: docs-faq
title: Questions
items:
  - question: Do I have to use the content file?
    answer: No. For a small static page you can write the copy straight into the HTML. The moment someone else needs to edit it, move the words into the content file.
  - question: Can I add my own CSS?
    answer: Yes — in your own stylesheet, using the tokens. Never hardcode colours, or re-theming stops working.
  - question: Is there a JavaScript framework?
    answer: No, and that is the point. Tiles register their own behaviour through SITES.register and stay scoped to their element.

### Tile: cta
description: Deep links.
id: docs-cta
headline: Go deeper
body: The repository holds the architecture, module spec, content model, theme engine, assets and integration specs.
actions:
  - label: Browse the docs
    href: https://github.com/MaryTheadoor/nown-sites/tree/main/docs
    style: gold

## Page: Blueprint
path: /blueprint.html

### Tile: hero
description: Authoring format.
id: bp-hero
headline: Write it as a blueprint
body: |
  A site can be authored as one Markdown file — front matter for the site, theme and
  nav, then one section per tile. Compile it to content.json, then build the pages.
actions:
  - label: See the compiler
    href: https://github.com/MaryTheadoor/nown-sites/blob/main/tools/blueprint.mjs
    style: ghost

### Tile: code
description: Front matter.
id: bp-front
title: Front matter
language: yaml
code: |
  ---
  site:
    name: My site
    baseUrl: https://example.com
  theme:
    colors: { background: "#F7F8FA", primary: "#1B3A5C", accent: "#2F6FED" }
    dark:   { background: "#0B0F17", text: "#E7ECF3" }
  nav:
    - Home: /
    - Services: /services.html
  integrations:
    forms: formspree
  ---

### Tile: code
description: A tile section.
id: bp-tile
title: One section per tile
language: markdown
code: |
  ## Page: Home
  path: /

  ### Tile: hero
  description: Opening band.
  id: home-hero
  headline: Your headline
  body: |
    A sentence that explains what this is.
  actions:
    - label: Get started
      href: /contact
      style: gold

### Tile: feature
description: The pipeline.
id: bp-flow
title: The pipeline
items:
  - title: Gather
    body: Fill the intake form — business, brand, sitemap, per-tile copy, integrations.
  - title: Author
    body: Write the blueprint. Humans and AI agents both produce this format, so either can pick up the other's work.
  - title: Compile
    body: tools/blueprint.mjs emits content.json and warns about unknown tiles or unregistered fields.
  - title: Compose
    body: Paste the tile markup into a page. Structure and CSS are fixed; the words come from the file.

### Tile: content-card
description: Run it.
id: bp-run
headline: One command
body: The compiler is build-time only — the delivered site stays dependency-free. It validates tile types and field names against the tile registry, so a typo becomes a warning rather than a broken page.
actions:
  - label: Read the format spec
    href: https://github.com/MaryTheadoor/nown-sites/blob/main/docs/BLUEPRINT-FORMAT.md
    style: ghost

### Tile: faq
description: Blueprint questions.
id: bp-faq
title: Questions
items:
  - question: Is the blueprint required?
    answer: No. It is a convenience for authoring and for AI collaboration. You can edit content.json directly, or edit the copy in the admin.
  - question: Can an AI write the blueprint?
    answer: Yes — that is the intended division of labour. The AI drafts the blueprint, the compiler produces the site, the owner maintains the copy in the admin.

## Page: Grid
path: /grid.html

### Tile: hero
description: Grid intro.
id: grid-hero
headline: The grid
body: |
  Two ways to lay tiles out. The automatic grid fits as many columns as it can —
  zero configuration. The configured grid gives you 12 columns on wide containers
  and 6 on narrow ones, and every tile declares its own width.
actions:
  - label: See the tiles
    href: /tiles.html
    style: ghost

### Tile: feature
description: The two grids.
id: grid-modes
title: Two modes
items:
  - title: Automatic — .sites-grid
    body: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(300px, 1fr)). No breakpoints, no column maths. Perfect for rows of equal cards.
  - title: Configured — .sites-grid--cols
    body: A 12-column grid (6 when narrow) where each tile says how wide it is with data-span. For deliberate layouts.

### Tile: code
description: Automatic grid markup.
id: grid-auto-code
title: Automatic
language: html
code: |
  <div class="sites-grid">
    <article class="tile tile-feature">…</article>
    <article class="tile tile-feature">…</article>
    <article class="tile tile-feature">…</article>
  </div>
  <!-- 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 columns, decided by the container. Nothing to configure. -->

### Tile: code
description: Configured grid markup.
id: grid-cols-code
title: Configured
language: html
code: |
  <div class="sites-grid sites-grid--cols">
    <article class="tile tile-card" data-span="4">one third</article>
    <article class="tile tile-card" data-span="4">one third</article>
    <article class="tile tile-card" data-span="4">one third</article>

    <article class="tile tile-card" data-span="8">two thirds</article>
    <article class="tile tile-card" data-span="4">one third</article>

    <article class="tile tile-card" data-span-sm="2" data-span="4">
      half on a phone, one third on desktop
    </article>
  </div>

### Tile: feature
description: Span reference.
id: grid-spans
title: Spans
items:
  - title: data-span="4"
    body: Three across on the wide tier. Any whole number from 1 to 12.
  - title: data-span="8"
    body: Two thirds — pair it with a 4 for a classic asymmetric row.
  - title: data-span-sm="2"
    body: Three across on the narrow tier too (spans of the 6-column narrow grid).
  - title: no data-span
    body: Full width, one tile per row. The safe default.

### Tile: feature
description: Alignment helpers.
id: grid-align
title: Alignment
items:
  - title: .sites-grid--start
    body: Tiles size to their own content instead of stretching to equal heights.
  - title: .tile--center
    body: Centres a tile's text and its button row.
  - title: .tile--end
    body: Pushes text and buttons to the end (right in a left-to-right language).
  - title: bottom-aligned buttons
    body: Buttons in cards, pricing tiers and products sit on the row baseline automatically, however much copy the neighbours carry.

### Tile: cta
